description: DeepSeek sparse-attention lightning indexer as one boundary: score[t, s] = sum_h weights[t, h] * relu(q[t, h] . k[s]) (x k_scale[s]) over keys ks[t] <= s < ke[t], then top-k positions. The joint score+top-k task of joint-indexer-ut.md (GLM-5.x DSA, DeepSeek-V3.2/V4); both the decode (paged, per-request) and prefill (ragged) branches.

n_keys.doc: keys visible to this call (context incl. prefix cache)

hooks.key_ranges: (name, spec, shape, dtype, sym, gen, device) -> {'ks': (...), 'ke': (...)}: each token's visible key window as served. Decode: one request's whole context (ks = request start, ke = start + context). Prefill: causal over the request (ke = prefix + position + 1). Reuse the observed per-request context lengths from the case manifest; do not draw them uniformly.
hooks.index_k_cache_layout: (t, name, sym) -> the indexer key cache in the layout the kernel reads (paged fp8 with per-block scales, or flat). The logical k stays row-major.

call: Invoke the joint entry (or the score entry followed by the live top-k, if that is how the deployment chains them) and return the top-k indices in token-row order. The decode and prefill branches are different kernels: one task with dispatch_ut/joint_ut phases, one regime per branch.

timing.cache: k is a long-lived cache far beyond L2 at long context; read-evict matches. The decode branch runs inside the CUDA graph: time it in graph mode.

negative_controls: drop the ReLU (or apply it after the head-weighted sum): many selections change, different_scores on most rows
skip the last head in the weighted sum: rows whose margin is small reorder
pitfalls: The score never leaves a fused kernel, so the selection is bounded against float64 reference scores with a small score tolerance: near-ties within that tolerance may legitimately swap, anything else is a wrong selection.
prefill and decode share nothing but the math: four different kernels across the two phases on GLM-5.2. One task must cover both served branches with per-phase regimes.
The prefill score is called once per run in some deployments; its e2e weight is whatever the observed effective_calls say, not 'prefill-heavy' because ISL is long.
Real key windows decide the work: a uniform window over n_keys misrepresents both the per-row cost and the tie structure.
